Pompeii and Herculaneum Brought to Light
New excavation methods will bring these two cities, destroyed by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD, back to light.
The backward peoples of Africa warmly welcome our benevolent government. Just as many Irish people once welcomed the British monarch, these blacks yearn for white rule (edition 10)
Around the World in 80 Days brings readers a delightful feast of knowledge!
What a day for the sick! Recently, our medical centers have been filled with victims of overly tight corsets.
A military airship named "La France" became the first powered airship in history to complete a round-trip voyage.
Skyscrapers are beginning to be built in the United States. These massive steel-frame structures tower over their surroundings.
Marvin C. Stone of the United States invented the "drinking straw."
A cure for morphine addiction has been found in the United States: coca wine!
Bismarck resigned as Chancellor, and the great ship of Germany has lost its helmsman.
Socialism will destroy Western civilization. Why? Because it grants power to the working class and makes them believe they will live better and richer lives. Bullshit! (edition 10)
Lynching of blacks has become commonplace in the heartland of America. Our editors cannot help but ask: should the state intervene or prevent such acts?
The Ader "Éole" was a steam-powered aircraft that made a short experimental flight near Paris.
The Daedalus glider became the world's first aircraft to successfully carry a person in flight, flying about 80 feet near Brandenburg.
At the Brooklyn Academy of Arts and Sciences, the moving images played by the film projector astonished the audience.
We believe that happier days than the present have never existed and will never come again. The editors respectfully propose adding the term "Gay Nineties" to our everyday vocabulary.
In this country, there are prophets who claim that one day humanity will fly through the sky using ingenious mechanical devices.
If he had wanted humans to fly, he would have given us wings. Shipping magnate and major shareholder of this paper Charles Orion commented. (See edition 10)

Renowned paleontologist O.C. Marsh revealed today that the famous elasmosaurus skeleton assembled by Professor Cope actually had its head mounted on the tail. The professor had no time to comment on this.
The first airship completed a test flight over Lake Constance near Friedrichshafen, Germany.
A strong hurricane struck Galveston, Texas, United States, causing approximately 8,000 deaths.
In Martinique, a volcanic eruption destroyed the town of Saint-Pierre, killing at least 30,000 people.
Mount Vesuvius erupted, and Naples was destroyed.
Earthquakes and tsunamis struck Messina and Calabria. At least 70,000 people died in Sicily.

A fraud disguised as a German army officer "ordered" soldiers to "arrest" a local council member. The man eventually surrendered to the government, saying he did it out of anger at the sluggish bureaucracy.
The RMS Titanic was the largest ship ever built. On its maiden voyage, it sank after striking an iceberg in the North Atlantic, claiming over 1,500 lives.
A North Sea storm struck the Netherlands, causing over 10,000 deaths.
Hiram Bingham rediscovered a previously unknown Inca city—Machu Picchu.
The famous German scientist Alfred Wegener proposed a theory that the continents we live on are floating on the Earth's surface.
Albert Einstein published his theory of general relativity, attempting to explain the relationships between space, time, gravity, and many other forces through very complex and confusing formulas.
Feminism will likely destroy the entire Western civilization. Gender equality will lead to the decline of civilization. Why? Because feminism will ultimately lead to female rulers (edition 10)
Crossword puzzles as a whimsical pastime will allow readers to demonstrate their powerful insight.
The death of the famous detective caused an uproar among fans. The author, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, decided to bring him back from the dead and issued a clarification to end the controversy.
Charles Lindbergh became the first person to fly solo from New York to Paris across the Atlantic Ocean (May 20-21, 1927).
Robert Goddard conducted the world's first liquid-fuel rocket test.
American manufacturer Jacob Schick received the first patent for an electric razor.
The Automatic Musical Instrument Company introduced the world's first jukebox.
The trend of sitting on poles has swept the Western world.
Television will surely destroy Western civilization. Today it's American Idol, tomorrow it's something super... (see edition 10)
Jazz will destroy Western civilization. Never in the history of music has there been such a corrosive rhythm. This jungle music rhythm has no place in today's oppressed society (see edition 10)
A new trend has awakened listeners' passion for music. Frenzied dancing, flappers, and folk elements are all byproducts of this novel music genre.
Presented by the modestly famous Irishman James Joyce, "Ulysses" describes an ordinary day in the life of the protagonist, a tormented, wandering Dublin commoner (continued on edition 19)
Today, more astonishing archaeological discoveries have been made in the Nile region, further fueling international fascination with Eastern things... (continued on page 2)
A brand-new futuristic architectural style called Bauhaus has drawn attention in cities such as Berlin, Weimar, and Dessau.

Two people—one fat, one thin—appeared in court, accused of pranks and various mischief. Given the seriousness of the case, involving property damage and donkey theft, prosecutors are expected to seek the death penalty for the defendants.
The vicious animal attack has shocked the community, and parents are demanding action out of concern for their children's safety.
As temperature records decline year by year, scientists warn that the next ice age is approaching.
He was hiding in a barn! After a thorough search, the missing child was found by local volunteers, hiding in an abandoned building nearby.
Yesterday, a horrifically mutilated girl's body was found tied to railroad tracks. The government is asking citizens to help find a man with a beard, wearing a top hat and black cloak.
A man claims to have witnessed a mysterious force—he saw a rabbit come out of a hat yesterday. He is currently being investigated on suspicion of supernatural phenomena.
A renowned prophet has peered into the distant year 2000. Speaking of the future, he said: "In the year 2000, every gentleman with land will own at least five hot air balloons."
An Irishman, a Pole, and a Prussian were arrested yesterday in an investigation trying to uncover a conspiracy to create fake news.
Yesterday, an angry bull caused the deaths of 5 men and 7 women. The normally gentle bull was eventually beheaded by a chimney sweep.

The collapse of a bridge near our capital nearly cost a butcher his life! The butcher is now the talk of the town. Fortunately, he was saved by his brother, a baker, and a young man who makes and sells candlesticks.
Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia, Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Albania, and Greece all celebrated the great peace that befell the Balkans last Sunday.
A reader is calling attention to those ferry captains who, disregarding passenger safety, recklessly push the throttle to the max and speed about desperately.
Next week may bring: rain, northerly and northeasterly winds, and a drop in temperature.
The fire department was criticized for lacking discipline and efficiency, allowing the fire to spread across multiple blocks, causing the largest and most devastating fire to date.

Police tell us that a thief stole a large sum of money from a local bank teller's desk. While the teller was distracted by the thief's accomplice, the money was cleaned out by the thief using a fishing rod and line in the blink of an eye.
Scientists claim that making children stay still is a form of torture. At this age, restlessness is children's way of expressing joy, so it should be encouraged rather than prohibited.

A new chemical process for hardening wood has been invented, reportedly making wood more durable than traditional building materials. Perhaps the city council should consider paving streets with wood?
Someone claims they can go 30 days without eating and still maintain physical and mental health. Shocked physicians say they will test the claimed ability.

A brig recently returned from the tropics, with reports that two crew members died of unknown fevers. They first experienced severe chills, then extreme thirst and hallucinations, until death finally came.
A European chemist claims that through a process known only to himself, he can coat ordinary crystal surfaces with a layer that resembles real diamond on all sides.
A poor member of our association received a charity letter marked "From God." His reply expressed gratitude for the money and reminded "God" to be careful of taxes and postal theft.
Top European doctors speculate that children's respiratory problems may be linked to increased factory smoke emissions.
Another "vampire frenzy" has broken out in the Romania region. Superstitious peasants have begun smearing garlic on their necks to ward off evil ghouls.
Wolves raided a town in Siberia last week, killing four residents. Armed police have been sent to the area to hunt down these beasts.

Terrible puppets have gradually been accepted as part of daily life. Recently, the existence of such toys has drawn attention again—a puppet called "Bimbo" has hit the market. Bimbo is a wooden boy with a frozen smile on his face.
At a drinking contest in New York last week, Irishman Bill Whelan defeated opponents from Russia and Scotland. From his hospital bed, he attributed the victory to "a great love of heavy drinking."
The honorable gentleman Jimmy Williams is known as the oldest living person. Williams, from the Deep South of the United States, politely asked our reporter to leave his lawn gracefully.
